meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I would like to be remembered as a person who wanted to be free'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely attributed to Rosa Parks and true to her life—but the exact wording isn’t in any documented primary source we could confirm, including the interview it’s usually credited to.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Universally credited to Rosa Parks and wholly consistent with everything she said and did—but the exact wording is not tied to any documented primary source we could confirm. The line is most often cited to her June 2, 1995 Academy of Achievement interview, yet that transcript does not contain it; the closest sourced statement is a differently-worded remark from her 1990 birthday. Treat it as a genuine but unsourced Parks attribution.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Attributed — exact wording not in a documented primary source

source.excerpt: I would like to be remembered as a person who wanted to be free… so other people would be also free.
trail: The exact wording circulates on nearly every quote site with no primary source—Goodreads hosts it under its standard notice that community-added quotes are “not verified.”
It is most often credited to her June 2, 1995 Academy of Achievement interview in Williamsburg, VA—but that interview transcript does not contain the line.
Wikiquote’s Rosa Parks page carries a related but differently-worded sourced statement from her 77th birthday (1990), not this one.
Quote databases such as QuotePark list it with an open request to “help us complete the source”—i.e., no source on file.
source.excerptNote: The line is genuine in spirit to Parks’s lifelong message, but this precise wording circulates without a verifiable first source.

author.name: Rosa Parks
author.heading: About Rosa Parks
author.bio: Rosa Louise McCauley Parks (1913–2005) was an American civil rights activist best known for refusing to surrender her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama in 1955, helping to spark the Montgomery Bus Boycott. A dedicated NAACP organizer for decades, she became an enduring symbol of quiet resistance and was honored with the Presidential Medal of Freedom and the Congressional Gold Medal.

misattribution.heading: A genuine sentiment, a phantom source
misattribution.intro: The problem here is not the person—it is the citation. This line is real to Rosa Parks in spirit, but the specific source it’s hung on repeatedly fails to hold it.

items.why: Countless posts pin the line to her June 2, 1995 Academy of Achievement interview, but the published transcript—including its featured pull-quotes—does not contain the wording “remembered as a person who wanted to be free.”

The closest sourced Parks line, per Wikiquote, is “I would like to be known as a person who is concerned about freedom and equality and justice and prosperity for all people” (77th birthday, Feb 4, 1990)—a different sentence that may be an ancestor of the popular condensed version.

misattribution.truthLine: The idea is unmistakably Parks’s, but the exact wording travels without papers: no fetchable primary source—including the interview it’s usually credited to—actually contains it, so we mark it attributed rather than verified (see Wikiquote).

context.heading: Why the line rings true
lead: Rosa Parks spent her life framing her own act less as a personal grievance than as a claim on freedom for everyone—a theme she returned to in interviews, memoirs, and public remarks for half a century. That is exactly why a condensed, quotable line like this attaches to her so easily and feels authentic: it distills a message she genuinely repeated.

The honest caveat is archival, not moral. A sentiment being true to a person is not the same as a sentence being documented in their words. Here the sentiment checks out; the specific sentence, as worded, does not trace to a source we could confirm.
detailsBody: If you need a citable Parks line on this theme, use a documented one—such as her 1990 birthday statement recorded on Wikiquote, or a passage from Rosa Parks: My Story (1992)—rather than this floating version.
context.pull: The idea is hers. The exact sentence has no papers.
